definition: For popular psychology, the belief–desire–intention (BDI) model of human practical reasoning was developed by Michael Bratman as a way of explaining future-directed intention.
details: BDI is fundamentally reliant on folk psychology (the 'theory theory'), which is the notion that our mental models of the world are theories. It was used as a basis for developing the belief–desire–intention software model.
story: Picture solving a puzzle by talking yourself through it out loud — wrong turns, second guesses, and all — until the answer clicks. It writes its thinking down, reads it back, and fixes the parts that do not hold up. Slowing down to think often beats answering fast. It is thinking made visible — the model shows its work, then reads its own work and improves it. That loop of draft, check, and revise is Belief–desire–intention model.
